summary:
SkyVale is an interactive space exploration platform that transforms real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations into accessible, engaging scientific experiences.

Astronomical data is often difficult to access and interpret without specialized tools or expertise. SkyVale bridges this gap by combining authentic NASA observations with intuitive visualizations, scientific analysis, AI-powered guidance, and collaborative exploration.

Users can explore infrared images, investigate how stars move and change in brightness over time, compare observations, and generate downloadable research reports. Guided missions, achievements, and AI companions make astronomy approachable for beginners, while advanced tools support deeper scientific investigations. Multiplayer features allow teams to explore and analyze the universe together.

By integrating NASA's SPHEREx data with astronomical databases such as Gaia and SIMBAD, SkyVale addresses the challenge of making complex space science data more accessible and useful.

Our mission is to turn astronomical data into discovery, empowering students, educators, enthusiasts, and aspiring researchers to explore the universe beyond visible light.
details:
SkyVale is an interactive astronomical exploration and research platform that makes real NASA SPHEREx infrared observations accessible to students, astronomy enthusiasts, and aspiring researchers. Our goal is to transform complex space telescope data into an engaging, understandable, and scientifically meaningful experience.

What does SkyVale do, and how does it work?

NASA's SPHEREx mission surveys the sky across 102 infrared spectral bands, collecting valuable information about astronomical objects. However, accessing and interpreting this data can require specialized scientific knowledge and software.

SkyVale bridges this gap through a guided, five-stage investigation process: Select, Discover, Explore, Analyze, and Report.

Users begin by searching for an astronomical object or selecting a suggested target. SkyVale retrieves relevant information from astronomical databases and NASA's infrared archives, including object coordinates, classifications, observations, and available measurements.

Users can then explore real FITS observations, adjust image visualizations, investigate infrared wavelengths, and interact with scientific graphs. Depending on the available data, SkyVale offers tools for studying stellar motion, brightness variability, and differences between observations. Findings are organized into a research notebook, with options to export scientific reports and data.

The platform also features educational discovery missions, AI-powered assistants, and multiplayer collaboration, allowing users to learn and investigate together.

What are the benefits and intended impact?

SkyVale makes astronomy more accessible by reducing the technical barriers between publicly available scientific data and the people who want to explore it.

Its key benefits include:

  • Accessibility: Beginners can investigate authentic astronomical observations without mastering complicated research software.
  • Scientific exploration: Interactive graphs, image controls, and analytical tools help users understand what the data reveals.
  • Education: Guided investigations encourage curiosity, critical thinking, and practical scientific reasoning.
  • Collaboration: Shared exploration tools allow students and teams to investigate astronomical objects together.
  • Research communication: Structured reports make discoveries easier to document, understand, and share.

Our intended impact is to encourage more young people to engage with astronomy and scientific research, transforming passive interest in space into active exploration using real observational evidence.

What technologies did we use?

SkyVale combines modern web development technologies with established astronomical research tools.

Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS provide the interactive website, investigation interface, visualizations, and educational features.

Backend: Python and FastAPI handle scientific computations, astronomical data processing, API integrations, and report generation.

Scientific tools: Astropy and related Python libraries support FITS processing, celestial coordinates, World Coordinate System (WCS) transformations, image analysis, and astronomical calculations.

Astronomical resources: NASA's SPHEREx observations are accessed through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). Additional integrations include Gaia DR3, SIMBAD, JPL Horizons, AllWISE, and 2MASS for astronomical reference information, positional data, and catalog comparisons.

Artificial intelligence: Groq-powered AI assistants help explain astronomical concepts and guide users through investigations.

Collaboration and development: WebSockets support real-time multiplayer functionality, while Git and GitHub are used for version control and team collaboration.

The platform is software-based and does not require specialized hardware beyond an internet-connected computer or compatible device.

What makes SkyVale creative?

SkyVale's innovation lies in combining real scientific research capabilities with the accessibility of an interactive exploration platform.

Rather than displaying astronomical images without context, SkyVale guides users through a complete investigation. Every stage introduces new information, from identifying an astronomical object to examining infrared observations, interpreting measurements, and producing a research report.

Its combination of NASA infrared data, interactive scientific visualizations, AI-assisted learning, guided investigations, and collaborative exploration creates an experience that is educational without sacrificing scientific purpose.

SkyVale is designed to make users feel like active investigators rather than passive viewers.

What factors did our team consider?

Throughout development, we prioritized scientific accuracy, accessibility, usability, performance, and educational value.

We considered the complexity of infrared astronomical data and designed the platform to explain scientific information progressively. We also focused on maintaining traceability to authentic observations, distinguishing measured information from catalog references, and ensuring that available analysis tools depend on the underlying data.

Because astronomical archives can involve large datasets and external service requests, we considered efficient data retrieval, caching, responsive interactions, and reliable scientific processing.

Finally, we wanted SkyVale to appeal to both beginners and more experienced users while supporting collaborative investigation.

Ultimately, SkyVale aims to make the universe more than something people simply observe. We want to give anyone the opportunity to investigate it, understand it, and make discoveries using real scientific data.
